Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray shows a large, well-circumscribed mass with homogeneous opacity in the right upper lung field, and the accompanying CT confirms a solid, non-cavitary lesion without obvious calcification or air-fluid levels. These features are characteristic of pleuropulmonary synovial sarcoma (PPSS), distinguishing it from the irregular/spiculated margins of carcinoma or the fluid levels of an abscess.
